title: Accuracy hides everything
sub: Move the decision threshold on a problem where only 1% of cases are positive.
legend: threshold: flag everything to the right

frames.caption: 10,000 transactions, 91 of them fraud (1%). The model gives each a score. Fraud scores (orange) skew high, normal ones (blue) skew low, but the curves overlap. Each curve is drawn at the same height; in reality the blue pile is 99 times bigger.
Threshold above 1: flag nothing at all. Accuracy is 99.1%, and the model catches zero fraud. That is why accuracy is the wrong scoreboard here.
Threshold 0.80: 21 caught, 70 missed, 4 false alarms. Lowering the bar trades precision for recall.
Threshold 0.65: 46 caught, 45 missed, 96 false alarms. Lowering the bar trades precision for recall.
Threshold 0.5, the default: catches 71 of 91 frauds (recall 78%), and 9% of flags are real (precision).
Threshold 0.40: 80 caught, 11 missed, 1,656 false alarms. Lowering the bar trades precision for recall.

Threshold 0.3: recall 98%, but 3,391 false alarms bury the 89 real catches (precision 3%), and accuracy has dropped to 66%. Notice which settings accuracy liked best: 99.3% for a model catching only 23% of fraud, and 99.1% for one catching none. Accuracy rewards ignoring the rare class; the right threshold depends on what a miss costs versus a false alarm.
